members.name: entropy_regime_v1
members.thesis: Shannon entropy of the distribution of 1-min returns measures the randomness/predictability of price action. Low entropy (returns clustered in a few bins) indicates structured, predictable market behavior — ideal for directional trading. High entropy (returns uniformly distributed) indicates random,
filters: No entries before 10:05 (need 50 bars for entropy computation) or after 15:10
None — entropy-based filtering replaces trend filter
weaknesses: Entropy computed on 50 1-min returns with 10 bins means most bins have 5 or fewer observations — the histogram is sparse, making the entropy estimate unreliable and sensitive to bin width choice
Low-entropy periods can coincide with low-volume lunch hours (12:00-13:00 IST) where returns are clustered near zero not because of structure but because of inactivity — false low-entropy signal
The 20-day historical entropy distribution used for percentile ranking may shift significantly during earnings season or macro events, invalidating the calibration
members.prior_art: Shannon (1948) information theory; Bandt & Pompe (2002) on permutation entropy for time series; Risso (2008) on entropy and stock market crashes; Hou & Li (2014) on information entropy and stock retur

members.name: maximum_entropy_v1
members.thesis: The maximum entropy distribution consistent with observed mean and variance of 1-min returns provides the least biased estimate of the true return distribution. When the observed return falls in the extreme tails of this maximum entropy distribution (beyond the 5th or 95th percentile), it is genuine
entry_long: Return_1min < MaxEnt_P5 (extreme negative return — genuinely unusual under MaxEnt)
close < vwap (VWAP confirmation of being oversold)
Rolling_Skew > -1.0 (distribution not too negatively skewed — left tail events revert)
entry_short: Return_1min > MaxEnt_P95 (extreme positive return — genuinely unusual under MaxEnt)
members.exit_stop: 20 bps from entry (tight — if extreme persists, exit quickly)
filters: India VIX < 22 (in high VIX, 'extreme' returns happen frequently, reducing the signal quality)
No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for moment estimation) or after 15:10
Volume on extreme bar > 1.5 * SMA(volume, 20) (volume confirms the extreme move)
abs(EMA(NIFTY_50, 20) slope) < 3 bps/bar (calm market — extremes more likely to revert)
weaknesses: MaxEnt distribution fitting with 3 constraints (mean, variance, skewness) on 60 data points is numerically sensitive — the optimization can fail to converge or produce degenerate solutions
Extreme return events on 1-min bars are often driven by single large orders (block trades) that do not revert — the mean-reversion assumption fails for information-driven extremes
The target/stop ratio of 30/20 = 1.5 with 57% win rate gives gross edge of 30*0.57 - 20*0.43 = 8.5 bps per side; after ~9 bps costs, edge is marginal at best
members.prior_art: Jaynes (1957) maximum entropy principle; Buchen & Kelly (1996) on maximum entropy distributions in finance; application to trading signals is novel but builds on established statistical theory
